The Core Collection

Four styles, always on the shelf, never out of stock.

The pieces that are always there tend to be the ones people come back for.
1 Kids Hat1 Dad Cap 1 Trucker Hat1 Tote Bag
Where this started

Availability may matter more than newness

  • From a $20 tote to a $290 one, four programs build it the same way. Erewhon. SunLife Organics. Alfred Coffee. Madhappy.
  • A small set that never leaves the shelf, with limited runs on top. Newness lives in the drops, never in the core.
  • Here it runs the other way round: drops, no core. 14 styles at Brentwood. 6 at Westlake. The second-best design never reached Westlake at all.
  • Appetite is not the problem. Have a Nice Day alone did 99 units across two shapes. The shelf is.

Erewhon

The ceiling
  • Two tiers, and they name the permanent one: the Standard Collection. Neutrals, original logo, restocked continuously.
  • Everything else is scarcity: Coachella totes, a Swarovski tote, Balenciaga and Merci collabs.
  • The tote does the work of a logo campaign. Highsnobiety calls it "shorthand for monied good taste."
  • $36Washable Kraft bagCore
  • $65Shopper Bag, eggshell canvasCore
  • $75Dad Hat, khaki twillCore
  • $95Market trucker hatCore
  • $290Swarovski crystal toteDrop
The takeaway

The core stays plain on purpose. Everything exciting happens above it, where it can sell out.

SunLife Organics

The closest cousin
  • A small, stable kit: caps, tees, hoodies, sweatpants, totes. The pink lotus sits identically on all of it.
  • One tote silhouette, sold as a place: Austin, Miami, Chicago, USC. The bag never changes. The town does.
  • Already proven here. Neighborhood dad caps took 47 units across 9 Brentwood territories, second only to the 5-panel.
  • $20Tote Bag, one silhouette per cityCore
  • $27Be Here Now truckerCore
The takeaway

Keep the shape, change the place, and one bag becomes a set. It already works on caps.

Alfred Coffee

The everyday end

A tight everyday kit, priced to be picked up alongside a drink. The closest thing here to an impulse buy.

  • $25Greek Cup trucker hatCore
  • $30Greek Cup Dad Hat, "We are happy to inspire you"Core
  • $32Logo mini toteCore
  • $32"But First, Coffee" tumblerCore
  • $50Crewneck / hoodie / sweatpantsCore
The takeaway

Two routes, one comp set. Erewhon sells a plain wordmark at $75, Alfred a hand-drawn phrase at $30. Both run here: wordmark on the dad cap and the tote, phrase on the 5-panel, the kids hat and the drop.

Madhappy

Where we want to sit
  • Their permanent line is called Core Classics. Their words for it: "signature silhouettes, assorted in a core palette." The thesis, already named.
  • Local Optimist is a phrase, not a logo. The message is the brand, and it runs across every piece they make.
  • Seasonal Classics sit on top. Spring Classics, New Classics. Same silhouettes, new palette, never a new idea.
The takeaway

The coolest brand in this set is built on a plain core and one optimistic phrase. Have a Nice Day is the same instrument, and ours already sells.

The proposal

Four styles. Always on. & never out of stock.

Core 04 · Bags

Classic Tote Bag

$55
41 units · 3rd

Tan oversized canvas, NEIGHBORLY wordmark, Have a Nice Day tag. Cost $25.95.

Priced to a real margin. The Classic Tote costs $25.95 and returns $29.05 at $55, a 52.8% margin, against $9.05 at the old $35. Totes run SunLife $20, Alfred $32, Erewhon $65. Ours sits near the top by design. Hat costs are still unconfirmed.
One mark, one place for it. NEIGHBORLY on the front of every cap, the place name stitched above the closure on the back. A new territory changes the back, never the front.

Retiring: the Yes Mom foam trucker (15 units), the Script and Varsity dad caps (11 and 8), and the NBRLY Blue Tote (7). 41 of 187 units across four styles, better spent as depth on the four above.
What comes next: the core holds all year, so anything seasonal reads as limited rather than as this month's stock. Every drop is a variation on a shape already above. No new vendors, no new samples.
